issues.failure_explanation: In Definition 2.2 (eqn: complex double layer), the complex double-layer potential is defined with the arc-length differential |d\xi| in the first integral instead of the complex contour differential d\xi. Because \nu(\xi)|d\xi| = -i d\xi, the real double-layer potential satisfies \mathcal{D}[\phi](z) = \Re[ \int_{\partial\Omega} \frac{1}{2\pi i}(\zeta(z-\xi) - \eta_1(z-\xi)) \phi(\xi) d\xi + \dots ]. Replacing d\xi with |d\xi| omits the unit tangent factor e^{i\theta(\xi)}, so \Re f_\mathcal{D}[\phi] does not equal \mathcal{D}[\phi]. Furthermore, the Sokhotski-Plemelj jump formula stated in Lemma 2.4(2) fails for an integral with respect to arc length |d\xi| because the jump acquires an extra directional phase e^{-i\theta(z_0)}.

failure_location.quote: In fact, $\Re f_\mathcal{D}[\phi] = \mathcal{D}[\phi]$, which is a function on $\mathbb{T}_\tau\backslash\partial\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In Definition 2.2 (eqn: complex double layer), replace |d\xi| in the first integral with the complex contour differential d\xi. With this correction, \Re f_\mathcal{D}[\phi] = \mathcal{D}[\phi], the standard Sokhotski-Plemelj jump relation holds, and the downstream proofs in Lemma 2.2(4), Lemma 3.1(2), and Theorem 1.1 hold unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The claims in Lemma 2.4(1) and (2) are false for the function as defined. Consequently, the proofs of Lemma 2.2(4) (determining the null space of \mathcal{D} - \onehalf I), Lemma 3.1(2) (injectivity of \mathcal{D} + \mathcal{X} - \onehalf I), and Theorem 1.1 (solvability and uniqueness of the Dirichlet BVP) are rendered unsupported without repairing this definition.
issues.title: Arc-length measure used instead of complex differential in complex double-layer potential
issues.why_classification: The repair is a straightforward local adjustment of the differential from |d\xi| to d\xi in the definition of f_\mathcal{D}[\phi], which completely preserves all stated lemmas, theorems, and guarantees without requiring new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: For any z \in \mathbb{C}, z - \overline{z} = 2i\Im(z), so (z - \overline{z})^2 = -4(\Im z)^2. Hence \frac{(z-\overline{z})^2}{8b} = -\frac{\Im(z)^2}{2b}$. Taking the real part yields \Re[f_G(z)] = -\frac{1}{2\pi}\log|\vartheta_1(z)| - \frac{\Im(z)^2}{2b}$, which has the opposite sign on the quadratic term compared to G(z) = -\frac{1}{2\pi}\log|\vartheta_1(z)| + \frac{\Im(z)^2}{2b}. The proof drops the factor of i^2 = -1 by asserting (z-\overline{z})^2 = (2\Im[z])^2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the sign of the second term in f_G(z) from + to -, defining f_G(z) = -\frac{1}{2\pi}\log\vartheta_1(z) - \frac{(z-\overline{z})^2}{8b}.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit complex representation f_G(z) given in Lemma 2.4(3) fails to have G(z) as its real part.
issues.title: Sign error in complex representation of Green's function
issues.why_classification: This is an isolated sign error in an auxiliary representation of G(z) with no downstream dependents; flipping the sign completely repairs the assertion without any mathematical loss.
